title: Vietnamese Caramel and Black Pepper Sauce
description: A small amber caramel gives this Vietnamese-inspired finishing sauce depth, with fish sauce, ginger and black pepper for balance.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: Red Boat 40°N fish sauce
ingredients.note: Estimate uses 1,490 mg sodium per tablespoon. Check your bottle. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

steps.title: Moisten the sugar
steps.text: Spread {sugar} in a small high-sided saucepan. Add just enough of {w} to wet the sugar, reserving the rest.

steps.title: Cook the caramel
steps.text: Cook over medium heat for 4–7 minutes without stirring until evenly amber. Swirl the pan gently if one edge darkens first.

steps.title: Dissolve the caramel
steps.text: Remove from the heat and let the caramel cool until hard and quiet, about 5 minutes. Add the reserved water and {ch} to the cooled caramel, then warm gently until it dissolves.

steps.title: Season the sauce
steps.text: Stir in {fish}, {gi} and {pep} and simmer for 2 minutes to marry the savory and caramel flavors.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over braised pork, chicken or flaky fish, letting the amber sauce pool around the food.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/2 tsp Red Boat 40°N fish sauce in place of 1 1/2 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the ginger and use only a small pinch of black pepper. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 32 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 7.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 189 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 30 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 7.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 65 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
